title: Anchored simultaneous gradient descent diverges on bilinear problems when the step exponent is below one half
description: Ryu, Yuan and Yin introduced anchored simultaneous gradient descent (SimGD-A) for convex-concave minimax problems, proved a last-iterate rate for step exponents p in (1/2, 1), and remarked that simple tests on bilinear examples show divergence when p < 1/2. We prove this: for every p in (0, 1/2) and gamma > 0, and for every rho in an open dense subset of (0, 1], the method diverges on the bilinear problem L(x, y) = rho x y started at (1, 0), with the gradient norm growing like exp(kappa k^(1-2p)). The proof reduces the iteration to a scalar complex recursion, isolates one complex constant that decides between divergence and convergence, and shows that it cannot vanish on an interval by a boundary uniqueness argument for holomorphic functions. This settles the statement divergence_for_p_lt_half in Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures repository. The repository contains the paper (LaTeX source and PDF), numerical checks and logs.
